Castoreum is the exudate from the castor sacs of the mature North American Beaver (Castor canadensis) and the European Beaver (Castor fiber). Castoreum is the yellowish secretion of the castor sac which, in combination with the urine, is used by beavers during scent marking of territory. Both beaver sexes possess a pair of castor sacs and a pair of anal glands located in two cavities under the skin between the pelvis and the base of the tail.

In the United States, castoreum extract is considered to be a GRAS food additive by the Food and Drug Administration. It is often referenced simply as a "natural flavoring" in products' lists of ingredients.
